docs.title: Why the Restore dropdown takes so long
Current result: batch selected-copy metadata in one CLI process
docs.text:
The selected-copy delay still came from remote calls, not file-tree processing. A fresh read-only trace measured 5,431 ms for three serial metadata calls and 2 ms for exact-response local replay. A later unchanged-binary baseline took 8,077 ms, illustrating the cloud latency variation behind the reported wait.

IncrementalRestore::verifyCopy now downloads the selected repository's repository.json and snapshot's manifest.json together using the documented multi-source filesystem download path... localFolder command. Both records still undergo fresh identity, schema and provenance validation before archive metadata is accepted or any entries are published. Providers without batch support retain their existing serial path. The chooser remains one request; selection with complete bulk archive metadata falls from three CLI calls to two, independent of the number of referenced archives.

Three live traces of the same 28-file point measured 4,053 ms, 4,804 ms and 5,280 ms for selection, with two calls and 2 ms local replay each. These are individual observations, not a percentile or guaranteed speedup. The two-second diagnostic budget still fails: batching removes one process/authentication/path-setup boundary but does not eliminate the remaining cloud work. No persistent cache, stale verification shortcut, remote writes or background prefetch was added.

docs.text: Three independently owned runners reduced some selections to 2,642–3,734 ms, but live testing also reproduced early failures containing database/lock errors. One failed bulk listing then triggered individual metadata fallbacks and took 6,216 ms. The parallel experiment was removed; the final implementation keeps the existing single-operation, single-CLI-process execution model. Offline overlap tests alone were not sufficient evidence of real CLI compatibility.

docs.title: Regression evidence
docs.text:
The request-count regression first failed with three calls instead of two. Coverage now asserts the exact paired metadata paths, cancellation immediately after the batch, bulk-list fallback, missing/changed archives, fresh verification gating, metadata/provenance rejection, one-command download output, partial transfer cleanup, basename collisions and preservation of existing local files. The paired-read/cancellation regression passed 20/20 repeated offline runs. The subprocess worker fixture previously handled only the final download source; it now accepts the CLI's multi-source contract too. Both manual and scheduled worker/restore integration rows passed after that fixture correction.

Final validation: cmake --build build -j2 succeeded, and env TMPDIR=/tmp/opencode ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j2 passed 41/41 targets in 361.21 seconds. git diff --check passed.

docs.title: Previous result: candidates first, bulk archive verification
docs.text:
The user approved showing unverified restore-point candidates before downloading their manifests. Normal selected-backup browsing now uses IncrementalRestore::listSnapshotCandidates: one safe, scoped directory listing. Candidates are labelled not verified and use a provisional folder date. Missing/incomplete points can appear, but listing never makes them restorable. Selection still freshly validates repository identity, manifest schema/provenance and archive metadata before enabling Restore. The validated listSnapshots and BackupCatalog::listHistory APIs remain available internally.

Archive metadata checks now reuse the existing operation-local RemoteMetadataCache, obtaining content sizes in one directory listing where supported. Missing, ambiguous or storage-only metadata falls back to individual inspection; trusted checksum requirements remain unchanged. No archive bytes are downloaded for browsing, and actual restores retain full hash/inventory checks.

A read-only trace of two points, 3,933 files and 14 referenced archives measured:

Boundary Before After Requests before → after Initial point list 11,321 ms 1,248 ms 4 → 1 Selected point's verified file list 37,987 ms 7,545 ms 16 → 3

Cloud timings are individual observations, not percentile guarantees. File loading still exceeds the diagnostic two-second budget because its three fresh metadata requests remain serial. Exact-response replay after the change took 0 ms for the candidate list and 255 ms for selection at millisecond resolution. An offscreen Qt Quick probe displaying the captured file paths built 5,147 tree rows in 117 ms synchronously and reached its next rendered frame in 125 ms. It measures Qt's offscreen rendering, not physical display latency; rendering was not the observed multi-second bottleneck.

The controller regression first failed at four calls instead of one, and shared archive verification failed at five calls instead of three for a three-archive fixture. Coverage also checks incomplete/malformed candidates, foreign identities, restore-eligibility gating, bulk fallback, unavailable archives, cancellation and preserved internal validated-history behavior.

Validation after rebuilding all targets: 41/41 CTest targets passed in 238.53 seconds. The controller target has 55 passing cases and incremental restore has 46; the candidate UI and captured-tree rendering probes also passed.

Temporary diagnostic sources are /tmp/opencode/restore-selection-latency-probe.cpp and /tmp/opencode/restore-ui-probe/tst_restore_render.qml. They are not installed application commands. The network probe permits only read-only filesystem calls; raw responses remain in memory and paths/credentials are not printed.

docs.text:
Selected-backup history now reads only that backup's incremental snapshots. Old-format copies are intentionally excluded from the chooser, as agreed; no remote copies are deleted. General discovery, legacy readers, retention, and selected-copy verification remain available internally.

flowchart TD

    B --> C[Download and validate repository identity: 1 CLI call]
    C --> D[Download and validate each snapshot manifest: N CLI calls]

For the same two live restore points, the updated diagnostic measured:

Exactly 4 CLI calls, 2 restore points, 0 errors. Replaying the same responses locally took 4 ms; reopening the loaded context took 0 ms at millisecond resolution with no requests. The original trace below took 27,472 ms. These are individual cloud traces, not a guaranteed latency reduction; the updated path still exceeds the diagnostic two-second budget. No persistent local cache or new remote index was introduced.

The offline CLI regression initially failed with 15 calls instead of 4 on a mixed-history fixture, then passed with four after the implementation. It also checks fresh verification on selection, zero-request same-context reopening, four-request refresh, and that ignored legacy copies remain on disk.

The implementation lives in IncrementalRestore::listSnapshots, reached through BackupCatalog::listHistory when the controller supplies a shared set ID. It reuses the private manifest/provenance loader, with the validated identity scoped to this single operation. Independent Standards and Spec reviews reported no findings. Regression coverage includes malformed repository identities and manifests, unsafe roots and snapshot entries, cancellation, identity refresh, missing snapshot manifests, and preserved legacy-format compatibility readers.

docs.title: Finding
docs.text:
The bottleneck is serial Proton CLI work during history discovery, not dropdown rendering or C++ container processing. On 2026-10-24, listing two restore points for the first locally configured backup took 27.472 seconds. Its 14 CLI calls accounted for 27.457 seconds, or approximately 99.95% of the measured time.

The original investigation measured the working tree including its pre-existing uncommitted restore optimizations, before the implementation summarized above. Backup names, remote paths, identifiers, credentials, and raw CLI responses are omitted from this report.

docs.title: Original flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as Main.qml / RestorePanel.qml
    participant Controller as BackupRestoreController
    participant Catalog as BackupCatalog
    participant Incremental as IncrementalRestore
    participant CLI as ProtonProvider / proton-drive

    User->>UI: Restore copies…
    UI->>Controller: discover(configured root, set ID, history=true, refresh=false)
    alt Successful list already loaded for the same context
        Controller-->>UI: Reuse cached list, no CLI calls
    else First open / refresh / different context
        Controller->>Catalog: listHistory(root, expected shared set ID)
        Note over Controller,Catalog: Background task; only one controller operation at a time
        Catalog->>CLI: list root
        Catalog->>CLI: list sets
        loop Repository directories, serially
            Catalog->>CLI: list repository directory
            alt Selected repository
                Catalog->>CLI: list snapshots directory
                loop Each saved snapshot, serially
                    Catalog->>CLI: list snapshot directory
                    Catalog->>Incremental: describeCopy(snapshot)
                    Incremental->>CLI: download repository.json
                    Note over Incremental,CLI: Same anchor downloaded again for each snapshot
                    Incremental->>CLI: download manifest.json
                    Incremental->>Incremental: Validate manifest and provenance
                end
            else Other repository
                Note over Catalog,CLI: Pruned AFTER its directory listing
            end
        end
        Catalog-->>Controller: Entire discovered list
        Controller-->>UI: copiesChanged; populate ComboBox
    end
    User->>UI: Select a restore point
    UI->>Controller: selectCopy(index)
    Note over Controller,CLI: Separate phase: reload metadata and verify selected copy payloads

The dropdown is bound to controller.copies. There is no incremental publication while discovery is running: first-open options arrive when the complete task finishes. Moving work to a background thread keeps the UI responsive, but does not shorten the wait for those options.

docs.title: Measured evidence
docs.text:
A temporary, read-only C++ harness links the same omacustos-controllers and omacustos-core libraries as the application. It invokes the real controller without QML, using the configured Proton binary and the first configured backup. Its runner permits only filesystem list, info, and download.

The harness records CLI duration and keeps responses and downloaded metadata in memory. A fresh controller then replays exactly the same requests and bytes without launching the CLI. Replay still executes provider JSON parsing, manifest validation, catalog traversal, sorting, and controller publication.

Scenario CLI calls Restore points Time Normal configured-root discovery 14 2 27,472 ms Exact-response local replay of normal discovery 0 2 5 ms Same-context reopen after normal discovery 0 2 0 ms at millisecond resolution Discovery rooted at this set's snapshots directory 7 2 17,294 ms Exact-response local replay of narrowed discovery 0 2 5 ms Same-context reopen after narrowed discovery 0 2 0 ms at millisecond resolution

The narrowed experiment changes only the discovery root supplied to the controller; production code is unchanged. It proves seven calls can be avoided for these two incremental snapshots. It is not a complete replacement for mixed legacy/incremental history discovery.

Both cloud runs exceeded a diagnostic 2,000 ms dropdown-loading budget. This is a diagnostic threshold, not an existing project requirement. Cloud latency varies; these are individual traces, not a percentile benchmark. Do not interpret the 10.178-second difference as a guaranteed optimization speedup.

docs.text:
Work Calls Total List configured root and sets 2 3,037 ms List selected repository and its snapshots directory 2 3,124 ms List the two snapshot directories 2 2,290 ms Download the same repository.json twice 2 5,877 ms Download the two snapshot manifests 2 4,951 ms List four unrelated repository directories 4 8,178 ms Total 14 27,457 ms

Both restore points had already been described before the final four unrelated repository listings. The controller nevertheless waited another 8.178 seconds before publishing the dropdown list.

The anchor was only 261 bytes; the manifests were 10,554 and 11,038 bytes. Small metadata downloads still took seconds. These timings include CLI startup and everything the CLI does internally; they do not isolate network, authentication, cryptography, or process startup from one another.

No archive payload was downloaded or inspected to fill the dropdown. Archive verification after selecting a restore point is a different latency boundary. The probe does not measure QML painting or physical screen presentation, but it reproduces the long wait before the UI can receive its model.

docs.title: Changes considered during diagnosis
docs.text:
Items 1–3 informed the implementation. The user chose to skip old-format copies in the normal chooser rather than add separate legacy discovery. Items 4–5 were not implemented.

  1. Separate selected-set browsing from full-root discovery. Derive the known incremental repository from the selected set ID and list its snapshots directly. Preserve historical v1–v3 copies through a scoped legacy path or explicit broader discovery. Do not silently drop historical copies.
  2. Read the repository anchor once per listing operation. Reuse that validated identity across snapshots of the same repository, while validating each snapshot against it. Do not make ownership metadata permanently trusted or reuse listing metadata as authorization to restore or delete.
  3. Avoid listing inside every snapshot just to find its manifest. The snapshot directory listing already gives candidate snapshot paths; read each exact manifest.json and handle missing/incomplete candidates safely. Preserve the existing provenance, identity, and path validation.
  4. Publish usable results before unrelated discovery finishes. If broad legacy discovery remains necessary, show validated selected-set results first and merge subsequent results by stable copy path. Keep restore eligibility behind fresh selected-copy verification.
  5. Only then consider bounded concurrent metadata fetches. The existing controller intentionally serializes provider calls. Increasing its thread count blindly risks shared state and navigation/restore correctness. Any concurrency needs independently owned runners/providers, cancellation, and generation-safe publication.

For this two-snapshot incremental example, direct snapshot listing, one shared anchor read, and two manifest downloads would require 4 CLI calls instead of 14, excluding any separate legacy discovery or existence probes. This is a request-count estimate, not a measured implementation or a promise of subsecond loading: even four serial CLI calls may still take several seconds.

The existing working-tree changes already avoid descending into object and bookkeeping trees and reuse a loaded list when reopening the same context. They do not eliminate the first-open scan measured here. Switching contexts or restarting is not equivalent to the measured same-context cache hit.

docs.title: Storage, power, and resource settings
docs.text:
Setting When to change it Remote folder You need a location other than /my-files/backups. Avoid changing existing repositories casually; see the manual first. Copies to keep You need more or fewer historical saved states. Cleanup still requires approval. AC power only Avoid running backups on battery. Staging directory Temporary disk space is insufficient; choose a disk-backed location outside your sources. Leave blank for automatic selection. Staging budget Adjust temporary preparation space; the default is 1 GB (1000000000 bytes). Resource usage (all backups) Reduce CPU/disk priority if backups affect desktop use. Save to apply to the next worker; a running backup keeps its limits.

Large files stay whole and can exceed the normal staging budget. Free space or choose another staging disk, save, then Resume. RAM-backed locations such as Omarchy's /tmp are rejected. Backups use compressed archives; there is no format or compression-level selector.

Leave Use system defaults checked for normal resource scheduling. Resource presets apply to all backups, not the desktop UI, and are not in settings exports.

Storage and staging details · Resource usage

docs.title: Pause, resume, or cancel a backup
docs.text:
Control Effect Pause Stops the transfer, releases temporary payloads, and keeps verified progress. Scheduling respects the pause. Resume Re-scans the selection and continues the unfinished copy. New/changed files are included; deleted/excluded files are omitted. Cancel Ends that attempt permanently. The next backup starts a new copy. Run details retain partial remote paths for review. Close the window The systemd backup worker continues; this is not Pause or Cancel.

Transient failures retry with backoff. Sign-in, power, and staging problems can leave a backup waiting for your action. Verified progress is preserved, but a copy is not restorable until its final metadata and data pass verification.

docs.title: 8. Other controls and settings
docs.text:
Choose the task you need. Top-right ⋯ contains app-wide actions; card ⋯ contains actions for one backup set.

  • Choose files and selection rules

  • Pause, resume, or cancel a backup

  • Understand backup results

  • Storage, power, and resource settings

  • Templates, appearance, and uninstalling

docs.title: Templates, appearance, and uninstalling
docs.text:
• Top-right ⋯ → Download template saves an annotated JSON example, even offline. Edit full source paths, unique IDs, and schedules, then import it. Imported template sets also stay paused and read-only until explicitly handed off and resumed. Template and examples · Generate settings with an LLM.
  • Appearance: follows the active Omarchy theme automatically; other desktops use the system Qt palette.
  • Uninstall: stop scheduling, then remove the package:
systemctl --user disable --now omacustos.timer
sudo pacman -Rns omacustos-git

Local configuration, resource settings, and remote backups remain.

docs.title: 2. Create your first backup set
docs.text:
A backup set is a named selection of files, with its own settings and schedule. A saved copy (or restore point) is a version you can restore later.

  1. Press Create your first backup set, or top-right ⋯ → New backup set.
  2. Name it, for example Documents.
  3. Press + under Source files and folders and choose your files or folders.
  4. Leave the defaults for now. Add exclusions if needed (examples below).
  5. Press Preview and check the Included, Excluded, Skipped, and Missing lists. Only included files will be attempted.
  6. Press Save, then Back up now on the set's dashboard card.
Example: Projects
├── Sources:       /home/alex/projects
├── Exclusions:    node_modules
│                  vendor
├── Include only:  [blank = everything else]
└── Preview → Save → Back up now

Tip

Hidden files such as .env and .git are included. Symbolic links are not followed. Check Preview before your first run and after changing your selection.

docs.title: What happens on later backups?
docs.text:
Run What OmaCustos saves First backup Everything selected: the initial baseline. Files added or changed New contents; unchanged data is reused. Changed files upload whole. Nothing changed Successful check; no saved change — no new restore point.

The default location is /my-files/backups in Proton Drive. The default history policy keeps the latest three saved states, but extra history is not removed until you approve cleanup.

docs.title: Moving backup work to another computer
docs.text:
Only needed to continue writing backups, not to restore files.

  1. Import your settings and correct source paths with Edit settings.
  2. Permanently disable the old computer's writer: processes, schedules, retries, and its ability to restart or access the repository.
  3. On the new computer, use card ⋯ → Offline writer takeover… for each set.
  4. Resolve any reported blockers; do not clear maintenance records to force a takeover.
  5. Press Resume separately for each imported set when ready.

Warning

Takeover is an offline agreement, not a server-enforced lock. Never let two computers write the same set. Taking ownership does not itself start a backup or resume its schedule.

docs.title: 7. Manage history and free space
docs.text:
Use card ⋯ → Review incremental cleanup… when prompted or when reviewing old history. Review the exact proposed deletions before confirming.

Retention policy → Cleanup proposal → Your confirmation → Delete approved scope
                                      ↑
                          No confirmation = no deletion
  • Saved states share archives. Do not manually delete individual archives in Proton Drive: more than one restore point may need them.
  • Failed or incomplete runs do not evict older successful copies.
  • Scheduled runs never approve cleanup themselves. Changed proposals need a new review.
  • Unfinished integrity coverage or damaged/unknown health can block cleanup.
  • Deleting some old states may not free much space: partly used archives are kept whole, not compacted.
Action Effect Open latest copy in Proton Drive Opens the latest recorded copy in your browser. Use OmaCustos to restore files. Delete latest copy Legacy private-copy folders only; confirms the exact copy before moving it to Trash. Not used for shared incremental snapshots. Delete backup set Removes local settings and its schedule. Remote backup data remains. Export settings first if you may need the set again.

docs.title: 1. Install and sign in
docs.text:
On Arch Linux or Omarchy, install OmaCustos:

sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel git
git clone https://github.com/jcergolj/omacustos.git
cd omacustos/pkgbuild
makepkg -Csi

Install Proton's official proton-drive CLI separately using a package or release source supported by your system. The OmaCustos package does not install it.

Open OmaCustos for Proton Drive from your app launcher, or run omacustos. If prompted, press Sign in to Proton, complete the browser login, and keep the terminal open until it finishes. Press Retry if needed.

Sign-in button not working? Use a terminal

Run these commands as your normal desktop user, not with sudo:

command -v proton-drive
proton-drive auth login
proton-drive filesystem info /my-files

OmaCustos uses the CLI's login session; it never stores your Proton password. The sign-in button requires xdg-terminal-exec, available on Omarchy.

docs.title: 6. Check backup integrity
docs.text:
An integrity check verifies stored backup data. It does not create a backup or prove that files excluded from your selection were saved.

When What to do Normal use Keep backups running. They advance full integrity checks when due, every 30 days after the last completed cycle. Before relying on old history or approving cleanup Consider card ⋯ → Run full integrity check while you still have your originals. Integrity coverage is unfinished Run the same action again to resume. A check can need several passes. You suspect damaged remote data Run a full check and inspect the reported affected restore points. You want to test actual recovery Restore a sample file too; an integrity check is not a replacement for a test restore.

Full checks download archives and verify their contents, so allow time, bandwidth, and staging disk space. The card shows Checking backup integrity…; a notification reports completion or errors, without a percentage or ETA.

Important

Routine reuse checks can miss same-sized remote corruption. New uploads and restores receive full verification. If damage is reported, preserve your local originals and inspect the affected history. A new backup can save replacement data, but does not repair old restore points.

See integrity details and recovery for coverage limits and handling damaged history.

docs.title: Restore after a reinstall or on another computer
docs.text:
If you exported your settings to Proton Drive, you can recover through the app:

flowchart TD
    A[Install and sign in on new computer] --> B[Import backup sets from Proton Drive…]
    B --> C[Choose computer and export version]
    C --> D[Preview import…]
    D --> E[Merge or Replace]
    E --> F[Restore copies…]
    F --> G[Restore files to a separate folder]

Imported sets stay paused and read-only. You can restore without fixing the old source paths, having local run history, resuming schedules, or taking ownership. For continuing backups from the new machine, see writer handoff.

No settings export available? Preserve ~/.config/omacustos before reinstalling if possible. With neither settings nor local configuration, incremental backups also support advanced read-only recovery. That path requires the source-built omacustos-incremental tool, which is not in the installed package.

docs.title: 3. Restore your files
docs.text:
Try this after your first backup: restore a small file and open it to check that your recovery workflow works.

flowchart LR
    A[Restore copies…] --> B[Choose a copy]
    B --> C[Wait for verification]
    C --> D[Select files]
    D --> E[Choose a destination]
    E --> F[Start restore]
  1. Press Restore copies… on the backup set's card.
  2. Choose a saved copy. Wait for its metadata to be verified and its files to load.
  3. All available verified files start selected. Untick anything you do not need; folder checkboxes include subfolders.
  4. Press Choose folder… and select a separate destination, such as /home/alex/restore-test.
  5. Press Start restore. After success, inspect your files, then press Done.

Warning

A restore can replace matching files in the destination. Restore to a separate folder first, inspect the result, then copy recovered files back where needed.

During restore What to expect Required download Selecting one file can require its entire compressed archive. Progress stays still Large downloads and verification may finish before the file count changes; there is no ETA. Pause / Resume Continue within this app session; a pause is not saved across app restarts. Stop restore Stops safely; already restored files remain. Closing the app also requests a stop. An error occurs Use View issues, then Back to selection to retry the full selection.

docs.title: Using another computer?
docs.text: Recover after a reinstall or move.

docs.title: Understand backup results
docs.text:
Result Meaning / next step New saved state A new restore point was saved. Successful check; no saved change No change needed a new restore point. Incomplete A historical result with some verified files and failures. Inspect which files are recoverable; not every incomplete candidate is selectable. Failed / Retrying / Waiting Open View issues or card ⋯ → View latest run details for paths, reasons, and retry information.

Run details also show integrity health, last successful check, last saved change, and capacity warnings. The progress bar counts work/file attempts, not live upload bytes. A large transfer can remain on one step for a long time.

docs.title: 5. Make backups automatic
docs.text:
Click the set's name or card ⋯ → Edit settings, choose daily, weekly, or monthly, and press Save. Scheduling starts automatically for normal, unpaused sets. You can close the app.

Logged in + computer on → Scheduled backups can run
Computer off/logged out → Overdue backups catch up after your next login
  • If scheduling needs attention, follow the app's fix or press Enable scheduling.
  • To make a set manual-only, choose disabled for its schedule and save.
  • Monthly dates missing from a month run on that month's last day.
  • Imported sets need an explicit, safe handoff before you can resume backups.

docs.title: Choose files and selection rules
docs.text:
Open Edit settings:

Control Use it for Source files and folders → + Add folders or individual files, including hidden paths. Exclusions Omit unwanted content, one rule per line. A bare folder name such as node_modules excludes matching folders at every depth; a full path targets one location. Include only Narrow a parent folder to matching contents. .env selects files with that name at any depth; .env* also selects .env.local, etc. Leave blank for normal full-folder selection. Preview Review paths and included source size before saving. It neither saves settings nor starts a backup. Run it again after edits.

Include-only rules support names, paths, and case-sensitive * / ? wildcards within path segments. Exclusions win. New matching files are picked up on later runs.

Selection examples

docs.title: 4. Back up your backup-set settings
docs.text:
Do this after setup and whenever you change your sets. Backed-up files and backup-set settings are different things:

Keep safe Contains How to save it Your files Documents, photos, projects, etc. Back up now or a schedule. Set definitions Sources, selection rules, schedules, and settings. Top-right ⋯ → Export backup sets to Proton Drive… or Export backup sets to file…. Full local configuration Definitions, run history, and other local app state. Preserve ~/.config/omacustos before reinstalling. Copying it does not grant writer authority elsewhere.

docs.title: Save settings in Proton Drive
docs.text:
Choose top-right ⋯ → Export backup sets to Proton Drive… and wait for success. OmaCustos uploads and reads back the JSON to verify it. Each export is a separate version under /my-files/omacustos/settings/<computer>/; older exports remain.

Exports are manual, not automatic synchronization. They contain no backed-up files, Proton login, writer authority, run history, or global resource preset. Recovery uses the last successfully exported definitions.

docs.title: Export or import a local settings file
docs.text:
• Export backup sets to file… saves a JSON file. Keep a copy somewhere you can reach without this computer.
  • Import backup sets from file… loads that file and shows a preview.
  • Merge updates matching set IDs and keeps unrelated sets. Names alone do not match.
  • Replace replaces all local set definitions, not remote backup files.

Both local and Proton imports stay paused and read-only. Original paths are kept; OmaCustos does not substitute your new username or home directory.

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Problem First action Cannot connect to Proton Install the CLI or Sign in to Proton, then Retry. Scheduled backups do not run Check login/power conditions and press Enable scheduling if offered. Imported sets remain paused until handed off and resumed. Expected files are missing Check Preview, include-only rules, exclusions, and View issues. Backup is waiting Open View latest run details; resolve sign-in, AC-power, or staging-space requirements, then resume as appropriate. Transfer appears stuck Check the phase/current file. There is no live byte speed or ETA; large transfers may take time. Restore or integrity check fails Keep originals, inspect View issues or reported errors, and retry after resolving the cause.

For worker logs:

journalctl --user -u omacustos.service

Limits: OmaCustos backs up selected files, not system images or live databases. Capture is file-by-file, not an atomic filesystem snapshot. Stop applications or export their data first when they need a consistent multi-file backup.

docs.title: Archive backup acceptance (#44)
docs.text: The archive rollout is delivered by #45–#52. Fresh manual and scheduled copies use version-3 bounded archives; historical version-1/version-2 copies and unfinished individual-file attempts retain their original format.

docs.title: Acceptance evidence
docs.text: MANUAL.md documents gzip level 3, selective-download amplification, staging and the oversized-file exception, legacy compatibility, and full-copy daily behavior. The resource measurements in archiverollout.md are local fixture observations, not Proton network throughput guarantees.

docs.title: 45/#46: operation-owned selective restore, versioned manifest validation,
docs.text: immutable archive contents, and safe extraction. See singlearchive.md.

docs.title: 47/#49: bounded preparation across selected roots, whole oversized files,
docs.text: storage Waiting, verified Incomplete copies, and success-only mixed-format retention. See boundedarchives.md.

docs.title: 48: unique-archive download cost and selective downloads through the public
docs.text: restore controller, with QML selection/cost coverage.

docs.title: 50: durable archive continuation through pause, cancellation, process death,
docs.text: transfer failures, and checkpoint interruptions. See archiverecovery.md.

docs.title: 51: source edits/deletions/exclusions, stable root mappings, and missing or
docs.text: damaged remote archive reconciliation. See archivereconciliation.md.

docs.text: scaling, and byte-validated resource/compression comparisons. See archiverollout.md.

docs.title: Completion verification
docs.text:
On 2026-10-06, cmake --build build -j 4 succeeded. All 24 registered native/QML test executables passed with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen:

QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j 4
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -R '^workerrecovery-test$'

The first invocation passed 23 executables before the command harness's 120-second timeout interrupted the long worker test. The second invocation ran that executable to completion with a longer timeout and passed in 161.65 seconds. This records a split verification run rather than claiming the interrupted invocation itself completed successfully.

docs.title: Archive continuation reconciliation (#51)
docs.text:
Resume rescans the current selection and hashes every member of each candidate archive. Candidates come from the latest durable prepared or verified mappings, not from the current enumeration or grouping order. Persisted root prefixes, restore paths, and member paths remain reserved even after their source disappears.

A complete unchanged group is reused only after checksum-grade remote evidence: matching content size and SHA-256 metadata, or a bounded staging download and hash when the provider only supplies sizes. Missing objects are confirmed through a successful parent listing; provider/authentication failures remain unfinished. Changed, removed, excluded, missing, or corrupt groups are superseded by newly prepared archives. Old objects are not referenced by the final index, and unchanged groups retain their original identities without another upload.

An upload interrupted before verified checkpoint publication can be recovered from its prepared record. That record alone never counts as verified work. Current local hashes and positive remote content evidence must match before publishing a new durable verified checkpoint and logical progress. Normal staging-budget, oversized-file, cooperative-control, and storage-Waiting rules apply to these verification downloads too.

docs.title: Integration coverage
docs.text:
workerrecovery-test::archiveReconciliation runs the real worker and subprocess CLI with independently stored remote bytes. Its checksum and size-only rows cover:

  • same-size local edits; additions, deletions, and new exclusions;
  • reordered/removed roots and newly added roots with colliding names;
  • file-to-directory and directory-to-file replacements;
  • missing objects and same-size remote corruption;
  • completed uploads interrupted before verification, including subsequent local edits, remote corruption, and missing remote objects.

Every row interrupts finalization again after reconciliation, resumes a second time, verifies the same copy identity and exact current logical counts, and checks that unchanged archives are uploaded only once. Superseded groups cannot reappear from older journal records. Final indexes are loaded by the public restore controller; restored bytes/hashes and the exact file count match the current selection. No cross-copy reuse, deduplication, or historical repacking is involved.

Existing archiveInterruptionRecovery, archiveReuseStorageWaiting, and archiveControlsPreserveOnlyDurableProgress regressions cover controls, checkpoint failure, quota failure, bounded reuse downloads, and recovery on another staging disk. Archive storage remains internally enabled until the #52 rollout.

cmake --build build -j 4
./build/workerrecovery-test archiveReconciliation
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j 4

These fixtures establish local correctness, not Proton throughput measurements.

docs.title: Archive interruption recovery (#50)
docs.text: Fresh workers now use bounded archives by default (#52). Recovery reads the durable payload_format, so a replacement worker does not require the original opt-in environment and never mixes formats.

docs.title: Deterministic integration coverage
docs.text:
workerrecovery-test::archiveInterruptionRecovery runs the real worker against the isolated CLI subprocess fixture. It terminates workers at source preparation, compression, transfer, remote verification, verified checkpoint publication, and final-index transfer. Checksum and size-only providers are covered independently. Additional rows exercise multi-member archives, Pause, Cancel, transient and authentication failures, checkpoint quota exhaustion, and archive staging quota exhaustion followed by Resume on another staging disk.

Assertions cover the exact copy namespace, prepared versus durable verified counts, logical file/byte totals, recorded-format recovery, staging cleanup, no redundant uploads of unchanged verified groups, scheduler respect for Pause, terminal Cancel history, and no retention operations. Each resumed copy is restored through the public restore controller and compared byte-for-byte with its expected contents.

archiveReuseStorageWaiting covers a reduced staging budget and actual download quota failure despite available filesystem space. Both use size-only metadata and two-member groups; recovery must enter Waiting without re-uploading the verified archives, and later complete after budget/quota recovery or a staging-disk change.

backupengine-test::archiveControlsPreserveOnlyDurableProgress requests cooperative stops at preparation, upload, verification, checkpointing, and finalization report boundaries. It checks journal state and prevents late manifest success, then resumes. Existing run-store tests cover queue mutations and progress/outcome serialization; existing process-runner tests cover stopping owned CLI process groups.

cmake --build build -j 4
./build/backupengine-test archiveControlsPreserveOnlyDurableProgress
./build/workerrecovery-test archiveInterruptionRecovery archiveReuseStorageWaiting
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j 4

These are local correctness fixtures, not measurements of Proton throughput. Prepared-upload reconciliation and changes to selected sources or remote archives are covered by the #51 slice documented in archivereconciliation.md. Prepared groups require current local hashes and positive remote evidence before a new durable verified checkpoint; the prepared record alone never authorizes reuse.

docs.title: Rollout and deterministic remote-operation gate
docs.text:
Manual and scheduled requests use the same worker default: bounded v3 archives. Recovery overrides that default with the durable identity's recorded format. There is no user preference or saved-backup migration. Internal fixture overrides remain available for historical v2 tests and the earlier single-archive seam.

workerrecovery-test archiveRolloutDefaults covers fresh manual and scheduled requests for an existing saved backup, an unfinished v2 attempt resumed with the new default, unchanged historical index bytes, and mixed-format public-controller discovery. With the same 8,192 original bytes split among either 64 or 512 files in separate directories, both runs transfer four archives and one index. Verification/retention metadata stays under a constant envelope (30 commands, including historical-copy discovery and remote directory creation); public catalog selection uses at most eight metadata commands and one index download. No fresh archive is downloaded by verification/retention. These are operation counts at the real worker/subprocess CLI boundary, not a wall-clock CI gate.

Version-1 compatibility derives identity from a timestamped copy namespace inside the configured backup folder (v1 has no embedded provenance). Every payload reference must stay inside that exact copy; unscoped references and invalid copy timestamps are rejected. The scheduled rollout row browses/restores an actual v1 index through the public controller. recentbackupcopies-test versionOneHistoryRemainsBrowsableRestorableAndDeletable checks retention eligibility, whole-copy deletion, and rejection of a foreign payload reference.

The full CTest suite retains control, crash, quota Waiting, source reconciliation, Incomplete/success-gated retention, extraction integrity, mixed-format history, owned staging recovery, and QML selection/download-cost coverage. Prepared-journal publication now has a distinct phase, Saving prepared work (not yet uploaded); only durably verified members increment logical progress. Final verification: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j 4 passed all 24 registered native/QML executables; the real-worker integration executable passed its full recovery/archive matrix.

docs.title: Opt-in resource and round-trip comparison
docs.text:
cmake --build build --target largebackup-benchmark -j 4
QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 build/largebackup-benchmark --compare 8192 268435456 developer
QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 build/largebackup-benchmark --compare 8192 268435456 mixed

--compare [files] [original-bytes] [developer|mixed] extends the existing opt-in benchmark; the original large individual-file continuation benchmark remains available with its original positional arguments. Comparison creates owned disk-backed source, remote, staging, journal, and restore trees and removes them on completion. Both formats consume identical generated inputs. Developer files contain code-shaped records with changing module/record identifiers; mixed input substitutes deterministic incompressible binary content in half the files. These are synthetic representative workloads, not measurements of a real user tree. Scale the arguments for a larger disk/resource investigation.

The local provider retains independent remote bytes and verifies SHA-256. All logical files restore through the production engine and their bytes/size/hash are checked against the source. Archive groups use a 16 MiB uncompressed target and a 64 MiB staging budget so several groups are exercised with modest disk use. JSON output records scanning/selection, snapshot preparation, compression, upload, verification, prepared/verified checkpointing, final-index work, restore, operation counts, uploaded bytes, sampled staging, and process memory high-water marks. Staging is sampled at phase transitions and periodically, including simultaneously retained immutable snapshots and compressed outputs, not just indexed source sizes. Restore sampling observes private download/extraction workspaces. Sampling can miss short peaks and adds instrumentation overhead; the deterministic quota/peak-retention fixtures remain the staging correctness gate. Current RSS is sampled separately for each phase, backup interval, and restore interval, resetting interval peaks for each format. Samples may miss short peaks and current RSS includes reusable allocations/cache retained by the process. The additional rss_process_high_water_bytes fields are a cumulative process high-water mark, including the preceding individual-file baseline when the archive row is produced; it is not isolated per-phase allocation or a standalone archive RSS figure. Timings are single-run observations, not p95 or throughput guarantees.

Each comparison also recompresses the largest produced archive's exact tar stream with gzip levels 1, 3, and 6, streaming bounded buffers. Each level must round-trip to the same uncompressed SHA-256. Reported time includes inflating the original archive, hashing the tar stream, and compression; validation afterward is outside that timing. The shipping level-3 default is unchanged.

docs.title: Local fixture measurements
docs.text:
Measured on an Intel Core i5-9600K (six physical cores), 46 GiB RAM, Linux, GCC 16.2.1 / Qt 6.11.2 / zlib, Btrfs disk-backed workspace, 8,192 files / 256 MiB per profile. These exercise local copying and metadata hashing, not actual Proton throughput or network completion time.

Profile / format Backup Restore Upload + verification calls (each) Restore downloads Uploaded bytes incl. index Developer / individual 13.48 s 22.96 s 8,193 8,192 271,620,336 Developer / archives 5.87 s 26.60 s 17 16 22,940,076 Mixed / individual 14.22 s 22.86 s 8,193 8,192 271,620,336 Mixed / archives 9.07 s 27.09 s 17 16 150,961,580

Sampled simultaneous staging: individual 32,768,128 bytes, developer archives 17,926,277 bytes, mixed archives 25,924,462 bytes; retained backup staging after completion was zero. End-of-run cumulative RSS was approximately 52 MiB after individual restore and 66 MiB after archive restore. Local full restore was slower for archives in these observations: extraction/integrity work is a real trade-off, even while payload-object operations fall dramatically.

Sampled current RSS peaks (backup / restore): developer individual 51,359,744 / 51,052,544 bytes, developer archives 65,310,720 / 65,572,864 bytes; mixed individual 51,388,416 / 51,142,656 bytes, mixed archives 65,253,376 / 65,511,424 bytes. Sampled restore staging was 32,768 bytes for individual files, 17,926,149 bytes for developer archives, and 25,924,334 bytes for mixed archives. Final-index workspace samples were 3,185,008 bytes for individual indexes and 4,656,504 bytes for archive indexes.

Profile (17,040,384-byte tar) Gzip level Compressed bytes Recompression incl. inflate Developer 1 1,131,626 96.5 ms Developer 3 1,148,933 107.4 ms Developer 6 1,071,570 172.4 ms Mixed 1 9,135,721 248.8 ms Mixed 3 9,147,118 245.8 ms Mixed 6 9,152,087 294.0 ms

Compression ratios and speed do not improve monotonically on every workload. Here level 6 saved about 6.7% against level 3 for developer content at about 61% more recompression time, but produced a slightly larger mixed archive at about 20% more time. Level 1 happened to be smaller than level 3 on both synthetic groups, faster on developer content and similar in time on mixed content. This is evidence of workload dependence, not approval to change the agreed default or add adaptive compression/tuning controls.

See MANUAL.md for approximately 1 GB normal grouping, selective-download amplification, whole oversized-file staging, Waiting/Resume, compatibility, gzip level 3, and full-copy daily behavior. Incremental backups, cross-copy deduplication, and custom oversized-file splitting remain outside this rollout.

docs.title: Bounded archive groups (#47)
docs.text:
Fresh workers create version-3 archive copies by default (#52). The normal payload target is 1,000,000,000 bytes; OMACUSTOS_INTERNAL_ARCHIVE_TARGET permits small equivalent boundaries in the real-worker/subprocess fixture.

Normal preparation accounts for immutable snapshots and compressed output at the same time. The conservative compressed allowance includes 1% expansion, 8,192 bytes per member for tar/PAX overhead, and 65,536 bytes of stream overhead. Groups shrink to honor the configured staging budget. Related direct-directory members stay together where they fit an ordinary group; large directories split, and adjacent tiny directories share groups. Selected roots are not combined.

A file exceeding the payload target or normal working allowance stays whole in a single-member archive. Preflight requires its snapshot plus conservative compressed allowance, independently of anticipated compression. Insufficient space reports required bytes and the oversized exception. Normal and oversized write/quota/flush errors retain unfinished work and actionable storage Waiting.

Archive objects live in a reserved .omacustos-archives directory, separate from source member/restore identities. Each group is packed with gzip level 3, uploaded, verified, durably checkpointed (archive size/hash/membership once per batch, with linear per-file identity/evidence records), and then its snapshots and compressed output are released. Prepared checkpoints never authorize reuse. Resume/reconciliation is implemented by #50/#51.

docs.title: Regression evidence
docs.text:
workerrecovery-test boundedArchivesRoundTrip exercises five workloads with a 200,000-byte normal budget: incompressible total input above capacity, target boundaries and related directories, many tiny directories, multiple roots and reserved/hidden names, and a whole 300,000-byte oversized file. The existing quota fixture measures actual retained files throughout the owned attempt, including both snapshots and gzip outputs, and enforces the normal capacity. Only the oversized row permits a larger working allocation.

Each worker-produced copy is restored through the public controller as a cross-archive selection, a folder selection, and the whole copy. Tests compare exact bytes/paths, reject unselected destination content, and assert one download per required archive. Existing single-archive damaged-content tests continue to cover malformed archives and unsafe members.

boundedArchivesStorageWaiting covers conservative oversized preflight after a verified group, snapshot quota, compressed-output quota, and durable-checkpoint quota, and write/stream-flush input/output failures after a verified group. The flush fixture injects the libarchive close-callback error contract (the normal unbuffered QFile sink generally has no remaining buffered bytes to flush). The interrupted cases with verified work independently validate preserved remote archive bytes against the journal's verified checksum/membership. No final index or success is published on these interruptions.

Metadata and final index memory remain proportional to logical file count; this is a temporary payload bound, not a constant-memory assertion. Each fresh run still uploads a full copy. Selecting a file requires downloading its containing archive, although only selected indexed members reach the restore destination.

docs.title: Incomplete copies and mixed-format retention (#49)
docs.text:
sourceFailuresFinalizeIncompleteAndProtectSuccessfulCopies exercises source disappearance during preparation for individual files, a single archive, and bounded archives with either legacy or archive successful history. The surviving file is exposed by the verified Incomplete index and restored through the public controller with exact bytes; the failed path is absent from recoverable entries. The worker records its exact source path, reading phase, and reason, and retains the older successful copy despite a retention count of one.

archiveSourceFailuresWithoutSurvivors proves that source failure without any verified recoverable files is terminal Failed, preserves successful history, and releases staging. Existing archive storage/verification interruption tests cover unfinished Waiting/Retrying instead of false partial finalization. Catalog, retention/discovery, and recent-copy management fixtures cover shared archive verification, mixed-format browsing, and exact whole-copy deletion.

cmake --build build -j2
build/workerrecovery-test boundedArchivesRoundTrip boundedArchivesStorageWaiting
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

docs.title: Issue #43: large-backup resource and continuation evidence
Reproduction
docs.text:
Build the native CMake targets, then run on a disk-backed filesystem:

cmake -S native -B build/issue-43 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build/issue-43 -j4
QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 build/issue-43/largebackup-benchmark 877172 95323650798
ctest --test-dir build/issue-43 --output-on-failure

largebackup-benchmark is opt-in, not part of CTest. It creates 877172 regular source paths, with exactly 95323650798 selected bytes, in groups of 1000. Generated hard-linked seeds reduce physical source storage; each selected file is still opened, copied, hashed, uploaded through the measuring provider, and verified by the real backup engine. Staged payload bytes are actually written to disk and the provider reads/hashes them. The generated workload is private to the benchmark and removed on normal completion.

The measuring provider retains remote content identities, rather than another 95.3 GB local payload copy or live Proton data. Thus this is a representative engine resource/continuation run, not a real-cloud throughput or CLI-memory run. The public worker regressions use a real subprocess CLI fixture with independently stored remote payloads and verified manifests for end-to-end behavior.

docs.title: Recorded run: 2026-10-05
docs.text:
Environment: Linux, Btrfs disk-backed working directory, Qt 6.11.2, Debug build. /tmp was a RAM-backed tmpfs; no backup payloads were staged there.

The first invocation deliberately interrupted after 10000 verified files, then re-scanned and continued /copy/same-copy. At approximately 900 seconds, the execution harness's runtime limit stopped that invocation; the durable journal contained 820000 verified files. No final manifest had been claimed.

The benchmark's optional third argument resumes an existing generated workload:

QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 ./largebackup-benchmark 877172 95323650798 \
  ./largebackup-benchmark-WllAdU

That command was run from build/issue-43. The measuring provider's virtual remote identities were rehydrated from the previously observed journal for this harness recovery. This is an explicit fixture assumption, not evidence that a checkpoint alone proves cloud content. Separate subprocess tests remove/corrupt remote bytes and prove the actual worker re-verifies or re-uploads before reusing them.

The resumed resource run completed successfully:

Measurement Result Verified files in final manifest 877172 Verified selected bytes 95323650798 Cumulative payload uploads 877172 Batches 878 Maximum files in a prepared batch 1000 Peak prepared payload bytes 108672000 (108.7 MB) Default payload budget 1000000000 (1 GB) Selection/checkpoint RSS high-water, resumed process 1371062272 bytes (1.28 GiB) Execution RSS high-water, resumed process 1563324416 bytes (1.46 GiB) Final-manifest RSS high-water 3676766208 bytes (3.42 GiB) Final local manifest size 378938645 bytes Resumed invocation elapsed time 411756 ms

All selected payloads were verified, the final manifest passed engine validation and provider verification, and previously checkpointed files were not uploaded again on continuation. The benchmark checked exact file/byte/upload counts and both batch limits before returning success. Its generated workload was cleaned up.

docs.title: Metadata assessment
docs.text:
The payload peak is independent of total selected bytes, but metadata is still O(file count). Selection strings, durable content/mapping identities, collision sets, and the measuring provider's own metadata contribute to execution RSS. Manifest JSON construction and validation account for the substantially higher finalization peak. Per-directory provider metadata can exceed a batch when a remote directory has many children; batch lifetime bounds cache retention, not the size of one CLI listing. These numbers are process VmHWM, not service-cgroup memory, system page cache, or a proof that arbitrary metadata fits in 1 GB.

The selected data exceeds the normal 1 GB staging budget by approximately 95×. The 1000-file limit makes this workload's actual payload peak about 109 MB. The small-capacity regression separately proves total input can exceed available payload capacity: preflight free-space and per-user-quota fixtures fail writes deterministically without filling the machine's filesystem.

docs.title: Routine public-boundary regressions
docs.text:
workerrecovery-test executes the real worker, engine, durable stores, and a CLI subprocess. It covers:

  • bounded bytes, 2005 empty files across file-count-limited batches, oversized files;
  • write/quota exhaustion despite free filesystem space, and insufficient space for one file followed by recovery on another staging disk;
  • same-copy recovery after killed transfers/finalization and checkpoint publication failure; partial folder commands and manifest failures;
  • local same-size edits, additions, deletions, exclusions, root changes, missing remote payloads and same-size remote corruption, including size-only metadata;
  • Pause/Resume/Cancel, scheduler invocations, crash before control acknowledgment, cancelled namespace history, and a fresh copy after cancellation;
  • owned orphan cleanup with active/unrelated/source data protected;
  • reserved manifest directories, file-to-directory changes, and source-root namespace collisions without lost or duplicate restore entries;
  • exact individual source-read failures, verified Incomplete manifests, and protection of older successful copies.

Existing dashboard tests exercise control targeting/visibility, waiting reasons, staging-setting drafts, and navigation while work is active. Existing immutable snapshot, recursive-transfer, restore, manifest, reliability, and retention regressions remain in the full native suite.

docs.title: Offline Proton CLI filesystem fixture
docs.text: protonclifixture.h supplies a reusable ProcessRunner that produces real files in a QTemporaryDir. It is shared by protonprovider-test and protonclifixture-test. No account, network access, or installed CLI is required to run these tests.

docs.title: Checked contract
docs.text:
Checked on 2026-10-02 against the installed Proton Drive CLI cli-drive@0.8.0+06e8c605, SDK js@0.21.0+06e8c605, using only:

proton-drive --version
proton-drive filesystem upload --help
proton-drive filesystem download --help

The documented commands accept sources followed by a parent folder; transfers keep source basenames. The fixture deliberately does not accept a requested destination filename as a separate argument. This makes provider name-mapping errors observable in the resulting filesystem.

Operation File strategies Folder strategies Upload create-new-revision, rename, replace, skip merge, rename, replace, skip Download rename, remove, skip merge, rename, remove, skip

Upload replace moves the old file or folder into an isolated fixture trash tree; download remove permanently removes the conflicting local node. Folder merge preserves nonconflicting children and applies the file strategy to conflicting children. Uploads automatically skip files with identical contents, as documented. Explicit strategies are required; interactive prompting is not modeled.

list returns actual children, create-folder requires an existing parent, and info supplies activeRevision.claimedSize. SHA-256 is absent by default, matching the supported CLI metadata; includeSha256 enables the optional provider field. Listings default to encrypted-storage-size-only metadata to exercise the conservative fallback. includeListingContentSize adds activeRevision.claimedSize to file entries; it also includes SHA-256 when includeSha256 is enabled. omitListingMetadataName and failListPath exercise partial metadata and failed listings. The upstream CLI's commandFileSystemList.ts prints SDK node entities as JSON, and the SDK's NodeEntity.activeRevision can contain claimedSize; the provider enables bulk verification only when that field (or content size) is actually present and valid. The installed CLI's filesystem list --help and filesystem info --help were also checked on 2026-10-03; info accepts one path.

docs.title: Failure injection and scope
docs.text:
• failUploadName: fail before a matching file or folder writes output, including descendants of a recursive folder upload.
  • truncateUploadName: report upload success but write truncated matching content, including descendants of a recursive folder upload.
  • downloadFailure: fail before transfer, fail after partial output, report success with truncated output, or report success with same-size corrupt output.
  • uploadedPaths, downloadedFolders, and trashedPaths: inspect staging, cleanup, and conflict side effects.

This is a documented-contract fixture, not a complete cloud emulator. It does not model encryption, authentication, thumbnails, remote IDs, revision history, permissions, ambiguous remote names, or escaped slashes in node names. Rename uses a deterministic .1, .2, … suffix; the CLI help promises uniqueness, not this exact spelling. Revision creation models current content only. The fixture uses small files and whole-file comparison for identical uploads.

When upgrading the supported CLI, recheck the two help commands and update the strategy table and conflict tests together. Live authenticated cloud testing is separate from this suite.

docs.title: Regression coverage
docs.text:
The provider suite checks requested-name mismatches, application manifest.json collisions, payload transfer failures, verified manifest entries, and restored contents. Fresh folder-backup tests also cover one recursive payload command, mapped paths across multiple sources, hidden files, exclusions, immutable snapshots, whole-folder retries, partial results, and staging removal before verification on both success and failure. The fixture suite checks its own file/folder strategy matrix and metadata variants, then uses the real ProtonProvider and BackupEngine for failed size/checksum verification, partial downloads, successful replacement, unrelated remote-basename files/folders, final-placement failure, preservation of existing content, and removal of staging artifacts. Restore staging and atomic replacement fixes land with these regressions so the suite remains green.

cmake -S native -B build
cmake --build build --target protonprovider-test protonclifixture-test
ctest --test-dir build -R '^(protonprovider|protonclifixture)-test$' --output-on-failure

docs.title: Run the opt-in benchmark
docs.text:
cmake -S native -B build
cmake --build build --target responsiveness-benchmark
TMPDIR="$PWD/build" QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland \
  QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Fusion QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME= \
  OMACUSTOS_BENCHMARK_SAMPLES=50 build/responsiveness-benchmark -nocrashhandler

Run on the real desktop backend, with the window visible. TMPDIR must be an existing writable directory on the intended test filesystem. The default /tmp on this machine is tmpfs, so omitting it measures memory-backed fixtures, not NVMe/SATA I/O. The JSON output reports the fixture filesystem, temporary parent, graphics API, memory-pressure allocation, and cgroup memory events.

For a separate constrained/pressure scenario on this development machine:

systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryHigh=384M -p MemoryMax=1G \
  taskset -c 0,1 env TMPDIR="$PWD/build" \
  QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Fusion QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME= \
  OMACUSTOS_BENCHMARK_SAMPLES=50 OMACUSTOS_BENCHMARK_MEMORY_MB=512 \
  "$PWD/build/responsiveness-benchmark" -nocrashhandler

Choose CPU IDs available on the test machine. These are temporary restrictions on the benchmark process; they do not modify application or desktop settings. The allocated memory is touched, then retained for the scenario. Check the reported memory.events high count to distinguish actual cgroup pressure from an allocation that never reaches its limit.

The benchmark is intentionally not registered with CTest. Deterministic correctness/nonblocking regressions remain in backupsetcontroller-test, backuprestorecontroller-test, and dashboard-test.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Dataset: 20 saved backups and 100 direct copy directories per backup. One selected copy contains 10,000 real files, each with a 256-byte identical payload, and a production-engine-generated manifest. Other copy directories exercise listing size; they are not 2,000 full payload replicas.
  • 50 samples per interaction and workload. Report each workload separately; p95 is the nearest-rank 48th value of 50 sorted observations. No warm-up samples are discarded after interaction measurement starts.
  • Real Main.qml, BackupSetController, BackupRestoreController, BackupEngine, and LocalProvider operate on isolated temporary state. Auth, systemd/scheduling, browser integration, and resource-setting services are doubles. No user configuration or remote account is accessed.
  • Idle: no active transfer or scan.
  • Backup: the production backup engine repeatedly scans, stages/hashes, uploads, and verifies 10,000 files in a background task. A new pass starts after the preceding pass finishes. The reported pass count counts completed passes, not whether work is active. A count of zero can mean the first pass was still running during all interactions. The GUI run-history fixture remains the last successful snapshot; this scenario does not measure live systemd worker progress writes/polling or Proton CLI subprocess contention.
  • Restore: the real controller restores all 10,000 verified files. If a transfer finishes between samples it is reverified and restarted before the next interaction. Navigation can enqueue copy listing behind the transfer.
  • Scan: a real preview() request is dispatched inside the measured interval, immediately before the click/key interaction. This includes scan dispatch plus input feedback, so synchronous scanning cannot be hidden by starting the timer after it blocks.
  • Selection uses an actual checkbox click with 100 existing ticks in a 10,000-file model. The separate regression test exercises 10,000 ticks, offscreen delegates, return scroll, reordered entries, and removed entries.
  • Editor navigation starts at clicking Edit, with the overflow menu already open. Restore navigation starts at clicking the dashboard Restore button. Typing starts at key dispatch to the editor name field. Navigation checks local visibility/focus; copy discovery and verification completion are outside the navigation interval.
  • Timings end at the next Qt frameSwapped after dispatch/update. QtTest input is injected directly, bypassing physical input/compositor delivery. This measures Qt frame submission/event processing, not compositor presentation or physical visible-feedback latency. Event-loop/harness scheduling and frame pacing contribute to the approximately 50 ms cluster. These timings are conservative development proxies, not proof of the visible budgets.
  • Successful restore completion can close the panel before a navigation frame. The harness reports those samples separately as restore_navigation_completed_at_boundary, and reports disabled navigation attempts rather than pretending they passed a timing budget. It also reports completion during selection; no such samples occurred in the disk-backed runs below. Initial tmpfs probes did encounter this boundary, which is why it is handled explicitly.

docs.text:
The measured Qt submission proxies are below the 100 ms feedback and 200 ms navigation p95 budgets after the changes. They demonstrate the large-selection improvement and navigation availability; they do not establish exact visible latency on the specified two-core, 4 GB RAM, integrated-graphics, SATA-SSD target.

Keep #22 open for the originally proposed i5-6200U laptop run, exact target hardware validation, actual rendered/presented feedback measurements, and representative real Proton/systemd-worker contention with live progress state. The faster desktop, small warm-cache payloads, and temporary CPU/memory limits must not be presented as equivalent to that hardware or workload.

docs.title: Follow-up optimization checks
docs.text:
Deterministic regression checks cover the subsequent optimizations separately from the recorded frame-submission measurements:

  • protonprovider-test: backing up 100 files to /backups/copy uses 101 uploads (payloads plus manifest). Existing-namespace mode uses two directory listings and 201 metadata inspections. Fresh-copy mode with content metadata uses three listings (two parent checks plus one post-upload listing) and one manifest inspection. Storage-only metadata uses three listings and 101 inspections; partial metadata uses individual checks only for omitted entries. Across two payload folders, full metadata uses two verification listings and just the manifest inspection; unsupported bulk is attempted only once. Nested sibling directories share cached ancestor checks, with cache expiry after successful or failed operations. Removing an ancestor during upload forces full rechecking and a retry of the immutable snapshot.
  • protonprovider-test: fresh-copy verification rejects payloads removed, truncated, or same-size corrupted after the last upload, using both bulk and individual metadata. Listing failures fall back without claiming premature success. Verified progress, incomplete manifests, checksums, and single-payload staging cleanup are checked independently of transfer command counts.
  • protonprovider-test: verification of 100 files across two payload folders uses two listings and zero individual inspections when valid listing content metadata is available. Partial metadata needs two individual fallbacks; storage-only/failed listings need one bulk attempt plus 100 individual checks. Invalid/ambiguous/out-of-folder metadata, checksum mismatch, retention gates, and cancellation after a bulk call are covered separately.
  • protonclifixture-test: empty and multi-chunk restores cover size-only and SHA-256 verification, truncated/same-size-corrupt transfers, and preservation of existing destination bytes and staging cleanup. Restore hashing and atomic copying now share one read; downloads into unused private staging paths are moved.
  • backupengine-test: 100 files in one nested folder ensure only the copy root and payload parent. A simulated disappearing directory causes one recheck and retry, and every resulting entry retains its verified checksum. A deterministic 40,000-phase stream over ten simulated seconds permits ten ordinary progress saves, with separate forced file-completion and finalization samples.
  • workerrecovery-test: a blocked upload still persists its current uploading phase without another engine callback; termination/recovery and manifest-failure cases continue to pass with the serialized progress writer.
  • retention-discovery-test: scoped discovery uses one copy-folder listing, three manifest downloads (including a rejected foreign identity), and two payload inspections. It does not list nested payload directories or other computers. Removing the newest copy's payload prevents that copy from evicting the older verified copy.
  • backupsetcontroller-test: repeated unchanged polls do not publish run-state, cleanup, transfer, or dashboard resets. Progress changes notify transfer display independently; successful completion updates the recent-backup model. Malformed state retains last-good data and clears its error after recovery.
  • backuprestorecontroller-test: switching away from a 100-file copy while its first inspection is blocked results in only that inspection and the newly selected copy's inspection, rather than completing the obsolete 100-file scan.
  • Existing engine exclusions tests continue to cover hidden content, bare-name and absolute rules, and individual excluded-file reporting in the preview.
  • backupengine-test: cooperative preview cancellation stops traversal and discards partial lists; a later uncancelled scan remains complete.
  • dashboard-test: toggling with 10,000 selected files retains selection-array and lookup identity, keeps reactive counts current, and handles the swapped final selection correctly. Offscreen selections, refreshed path order, and return scroll remain covered.

The full 22-target CTest suite passes. These regression checks establish command counts and behavior; they do not measure presentation latency or end-to-end cloud backup speed.

docs.title: Manifest and CLI measurements, 2026-10-03
docs.text:
Run the opt-in manifest loader benchmark from the repository root:

cmake --build build --target manifest-benchmark
QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 QT_LOGGING_RULES='*.info=true' \
  TMPDIR="$PWD/build" build/manifest-benchmark

The benchmark loads valid incomplete version-2 manifests through the production loader. Each fixture has equal numbers of verified entries and distinct failed paths; its construction is outside the measured interval. Results include JSON parsing and validation, with one warm-up followed by five samples. The environment is the development desktop documented above, using the existing workspace build and disk-backed temporary files; these are warm-cache loader timings.

The baseline uses the same build and benchmark with the entry-validation lookup changed back from failedSet.contains(restorePath) to failedItems.contains(restorePath). Restore the set lookup and rebuild to reproduce the after result. All other loader work is identical.

Verified entries / failed paths Manifest bytes Before median After median Reduction 1,000 / 1,000 352,537 10.6 ms 10.4 ms approximately 2% 10,000 / 10,000 3,583,537 152.4 ms 107.2 ms approximately 30%

This is about a 1.42x loader speedup for the larger incomplete fixture, not a prediction that every manifest or entire backup becomes 1.42x faster.

Read-only measurements against the installed Proton CLI also checked the actual listing contract. The /my-files root listed five file nodes, four with content size metadata; omitted metadata still needs the individual fallback. After an initial probe, three root listings had a median of 807 ms, and three inspections of one file had a median of 756 ms. Initial probes were slower (approximately 1.4 seconds for root info and 2.9 seconds for listing), showing startup/network variation. These small samples are not a representative payload-directory or end-to-end backup benchmark. No cloud uploads or deletions were performed.

The deterministic fresh-copy fixture reduces verification of 100 payloads in one folder from 100 individual inspections to one listing when complete content metadata is available: 99% fewer payload-verification requests. Uploads and the manifest's individual verification remain. In the storage-only case, there is one extra attempted listing before the original individual checks; no speedup is claimed for that fallback.
